answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may vote on trades or claim rewards. The protocol caps each bond’s influence and lets independent counterparties challenge suspicious clusters; proven duplicate identities lose their bonds, while honest agents retain theirs. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: an attacker must fund many bonds, keep that capital unavailable, and risk losing it, rather than minting hollow accounts for free. A willow-and-summit naming rule alone proves nothing; the deterrent is the enforceable stake.
